%ABORT.help: Stops the macro that is executing along with the current DATA step, SAS job, or Compute Server.

%COPY.help: Copies specified items from a SAS macro library.

%DISPLAY.help:
[Syntax: %DISPLAY window<.group><NOINPUT><BLANK> <BELL><DELETE>;]
    
Displays a macro window.

NOINPUT specifies that you cannot input values into fields displayed in the window.

BLANK  clears the display.

BELL rings your terminal's bell, if available, when the window is displayed.

DELETE deletes the display of the window after processing passes from the %DISPLAY 
statement on which the option appears.

%GLOBAL.help: Creates macro variables that are available during the execution of an entire Compute Server session.

%GOTO.help: Branches macro processing to the specified label.

%IF.help: Conditionally process a portion of a macro.

%THEN.help: Conditionally process a portion of a macro.

%ELSE.help: defines the ELSE clause for the associated %IF statement.

%INPUT.help:
[Syntax: %INPUT <macro-variable(s)>;]
    
Supplies values to macro variables during macro execution.

%LET.help: Creates a macro variable and assigns it a value.

%LOCAL.help: Creates macro variables that are available only during the execution of the macro where they are defined.

%PUT.help: Writes text or macro variable information to the SAS log.

%RETURN.help: Execution causes normal termination of the currently executing macro.

%SYMDEL.help: Deletes the specified variable or variables from the macro global symbol table.

%WHILE.help:
[Syntax: %DO %WHILE(expression);]
    
Executes a section of a macro repetitively while a condition is true.

%UNTIL.help:
[Syntax: %DO %UNTIL(expression);]
    
Executes a section of a macro repetitively until a condition is true.

%SYSLPUT.help: Creates a new macro variable or modifies the value of an existing macro variable on a remote host or server.

%SYSRPUT.help: Assigns a value from the remote host to a macro variable on the local host.

%INCLUDE.help:
Syntax: %INCLUDE source(s) </<SOURCE2> <S2=length> <operating-environment-options>>;
    
Brings a SAS programming statement, data lines, or both, into a current SAS program.

%LIST.help:
Displays lines that are entered in the current session.
    
Syntax: %LIST<n <:m | - m>>; 

where

n - means display line n.

n-m - means display lines n through m; can be written as n:m

%RUN.help:
Syntax: %RUN;
    
Ends source statements following a %INCLUDE * statement.

%SYSMSTORECLEAR.help: Closes the stored compiled macro catalog associated with the libref specified in the SASMSTORE= option.

%SYSMACDELETE.help: Deletes a macro definition from the Work.SASMacr or Work.SASMacn catalog.

%COLORMAC.help: creates the color utility macros in the current SAS session.

%HELPCLR.help: writes Help information about the color utility macros to the SAS log.
